parts:
Hi Ben,

Sorry for his mistake. All required packages were probably already loaded in my session so I could not see the errors.

Also, I just noticed  that the date issue (question #2) was a poor statement of scale_x_datetime, which I've fixed. 

However, I am still interested in learning how to create a legend to identify the lines in this plot. Here is the updated, full reproducible code (still rather long due to data generation):

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
require(ggplot2)
require(scales)
require(grid)
require(plyr)
scale_x_datetime(breaks = '12 hour', labels = date_format('%b-%d %H:%M')) +

theme_bw(base_size=20) +
        theme(panel.margin = unit(0,'lines'), axis.title.x = element_blank()) +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
        theme(axis.title.y=element_text(vjust=3)) +
        theme(plot.margin = unit(c(1,1,-0.2, 1), "cm"))

# plot #1 - air + dew point temperatures
air.dew <- q2.p +
           geom_line(subset = .(variable == 'air'), linetype='solid')  +
           geom_line(subset = .(variable == 'dew'), linetype='dashed') +
           labs(x = NA, y = 'Temperature (°C)') +
           theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

# plot #2 - dew point temp. depression
dew.dep <- q2.p + geom_line(subset = .(variable == 'dew.dep'), linetype='solid') +
           labs(x = NA, y = 'Dew point temp. depression (°C)') 

pp5 <- ggplotGrob(air.dew)
pp6 <- ggplotGrob(dew.dep)

# Draw figure
grid.draw(rbind(pp5,pp6,size='first'))

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
Greetings,

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Create manual legend while plotting subset data frame
parts:
Hi Thiago,

So ggplot isn't providing an automatic legend because of how you've
set this up, i.e. the two geom_line calls in the construction of
air.dew instead of a single line like this

geom_line(subset = .(variable %in% c('air','dew')),
aes(linetype=variable)) +

More generally, I'd suggest looking at Hadley's slick example of how
to share a single legend between two plots:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/Share-a-legend-between-two-ggplot2-graphs.
That's how I would do it, anyway.

HTH,
Ben
